outcome: A working application restored complete, not just its volumes, with the resources and configuration needed to bring it back to life included.
overview: Teams running Kubernetes often believe their applications are stateless and discover, usually during an incident, that several are not: a database in a container, a persistent volume nobody catalogued, custom resources that define how the application is assembled. Kasten K10 protects the application as a unit — its resources, its configuration and its volumes together — rather than backing up volumes and hoping the rest can be reconstructed. It runs on any conformant Kubernetes, which keeps it aligned with the portability those platforms were chosen for.

benefits.text: An application is captured as a unit — resources, configuration and volumes together
benefits.limits: Application-consistent capture for databases requires hooks to quiesce them; without those, a volume copy of a running database is a crash-consistent copy

benefits.text: Protection runs on any conformant Kubernetes rather than tying the estate to one distribution
benefits.limits: Portability of the protection platform does not make the applications portable; storage class differences still affect restores across clusters

benefits.text: Applications can be migrated between clusters using the same capture
benefits.limits: Backup success rate is not recoverability; only a tested restore against a stated objective evidences it, and the two are routinely substituted for one another

residency: Copies land in object storage the customer chooses, in any region they control

notFor.situation: A genuinely stateless application estate with externalised data
notFor.why: If state lives in managed services outside the cluster, those services need protecting rather than the cluster

notFor.situation: An estate already protected by an equivalent Kubernetes-aware platform
notFor.why: Two protection platforms on one cluster duplicates snapshot pressure on the same storage

scope:
Model: Redington solutions engineering with an accredited Veeam implementation partner · Duration: 4–6 weeks to protected applications with a first tested restore
Support model: Vendor subscription support; Redington coordinates the vendor case.
1) Inventory — stateful applications identified, storage classes checked, hook coverage assessed
2) Design — protection policies per application, retention and object storage layout
3) Deploy — capture running across the stateful application set
4) Test and hand over — restore tested including into a second cluster, operations handed over
